turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's start with why my son found out about a zero from his phone, in the middle of class.
I'm waiting, Hale. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen spoken to before it went in?
We're not here about the weather. Who decided on the zero, Hale?
I'm waiting, Hale. The zero went in on Tuesday, November 3, and nobody called me. Who decided it?
Okay isn't an answer, Hale. The zero comes off, and I want an apology for how Owen found out. If you have nothing to say to that, I'm going upstairs to the principal.

I'm writing down that you had nothing to say when I asked who decided. Procedure 4.2 says a parent is called before any mark goes in, and nobody called me. Say something about that, Hale, or I'm done here.
Then that's my answer. I'm taking the zero, the missed call and Procedure 4.2 to the principal's office now. You can come with me, Hale, or I'll go alone.
Sorry. The essay quotes a line that isn't in Hamlet.
Which line, Hale, and where in the essay is it? A wrong quotation is an error in an essay, not a basis for a zero. Show me the page.
